items.title: `uv lock` errors if `.venv` is not valid
items.reason: astral-sh/uv#19832 is the canonical match: same reporter, command, `.venv/<version>` layout, exact error, workaround, expected fallback, and proposed `--active` alternative.

items.title: Added flag for whether to fail on invalid environments during project interpreter discovery
items.reason: astral-sh/uv#19833 proposes fixing astral-sh/uv#19832 directly by letting `uv lock` fall back to global or managed interpreter discovery when `.venv` is invalid.

items.title: Allow fallback to interpreter discovery for non-venv .venv directory
items.reason: astral-sh/uv#20333 was an earlier implementation of the same fallback for astral-sh/uv#19832; its author closed it without review comments.

items.title: Add support for respecting `VIRTUAL_ENV` in project commands via `--active`
items.reason: astral-sh/uv#11189 introduced `--active` for environment-mutating project commands but explicitly left `uv lock` using `active = false`, establishing the current capability boundary.

related.search_scope: Searched open and closed issues and open, closed, and merged pull requests for literal combinations of `uv lock`, `.venv`, `--active`, and the exact invalid-environment error; conceptual terms covering interpreter discovery, fallback, active environments, `VIRTUAL_ENV`, and `UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT`; and historical fixes. Followed astral-sh/uv#19832’s references to astral-sh/uv#19833, astral-sh/uv#20333, and astral-sh/uv#13235, and inspected the `--active` history in astral-sh/uv#11189. Ruled out astral-sh/uv#19885 because its same error came from an accidental Docker copy during `uv sync`, astral-sh/uv#11219 because its trigger was concurrent environment creation, and astral-sh/uv#17780 because it concerns sync-target versus project-root discovery semantics.

type_reason: astral-sh/uv#19832 already tracks the identical `uv lock` failure and explicitly proposes `--active` as an alternative remedy. The new issue presents the flag as a temporary solution for that open issue and adds no distinct trigger or capability, so duplicate takes precedence over enhancement.
summary: astral-sh/uv#19832 is the canonical issue. astral-sh/uv#19833 is its open proposed fix, while astral-sh/uv#20333 records a closed alternative implementation and astral-sh/uv#11189 establishes the existing `--active` behavior.
draft_response: Thanks. This request is already covered by astral-sh/uv#19832: it reports the same `uv lock` failure for a non-virtual-environment `.venv`, including the version-subdirectory layout, and already identifies `--active` as one possible remedy. There is also an open proposed fix in astral-sh/uv#19833 to have `uv lock` fall back to normal interpreter discovery instead of requiring a CLI bypass. Let’s keep the behavior and solution discussion on astral-sh/uv#19832, so I’ll close this as a duplicate.
